verdict.rationale: Phoenix's docs describe capturing traces of model calls through OTLP, auto-instrumentation and manual decorators. They also document latency analysis for slow LLM invocations and a detailed token-usage breakdown per LLM call, and a community user reports using Phoenix traces and spans. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that LLM spans record prompt inputs and completion outputs (this is only implied by span replay and response-generation capture), and hands-on corroboration of latency and token fields specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: A trace captures model calls, retrieval, tool use, and custom logic so you can debug behavior and understand where time is spent.
Application Latency: Identify and address slow invocations of LLMs, Retrievers, and other components within your application
Gain a detailed breakdown of token usage for your LLM calls, allowing you to identify and optimize the most expensive LLM invocations.
tracing can capture the sequence of operations, such as document retrieval, embedding generation, language model invocation, and response generation
Phoenix accepts traces over OpenTelemetry (OTLP) and provides auto-instrumentation for popular frameworks (LlamaIndex, LangChain, DSPy, Mastra, Vercel AI SDK)
